correctness.rationale: Conditioning on Pi(j)=j leaves disjoint-window ranks exchangeable; for a window containing j the conditional probability is the exact product of two binomial coefficients divided by (n−1)_{k−1}. Summing the j positions and applying Vandermonde over order statistics gives the boundary identity without any false independence assumption. For k=4, every boundary term is polynomial of degree ≤3. Exact evaluation of 24 printed polynomials at four n=4,5,6,7 values proves all identities by the degree bound. Independently recalculated all 24 polynomial numerators by integer boundary sums and signs; exactly three have both strict signs with thresholds 5/6, 17/18, 6/7. k2 and k3 closed formula signs checked. Supplemental exhaustive n≤9 moments do not replace the general counting proof.
